audit_scope.description: Batch 15 covers exception handling, error propagation, transaction validation failures, and network protocol error handling. Focus is on how EL handles invalid inputs and exceptional conditions.

misclassified_entities.reason: While P2P peers do trigger errors by sending invalid data, the 'Peer Node' entity in exception handling context is not truly external - it's the local node's processing of potentially invalid peer data. The actual external entity is the P2P network peer sending invalid protocol messages.

Transaction submitter in exception context refers to the entity whose transaction is being rejected, but from EL perspective, the transaction is already internalized when exceptions occur during execution. The external boundary is the RPC/P2P interface where transaction is received.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peers via DevP2P - Invalid Protocol Messages
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Malicious or buggy peers send invalid blocks, transactions, or protocol messages. EL must validate all received data and raise appropriate exceptions (InvalidBlock, InvalidTransaction). Invalid data must not cause crashes or consensus failures. Peer reputation systems may track peers sending invalid data.

trusted_external_entities.name: RPC Clients via JSON-RPC - Invalid Transaction Submissions
trusted_external_entities.rationale: RPC clients can submit invalid transactions (invalid signature, insufficient gas, nonce mismatch, insufficient balance). EL must validate all transaction parameters and return appropriate error codes via JSON-RPC response. Invalid transactions must not enter mempool or cause node failures.

trusted_external_entities.name: Smart Contracts - Invalid EVM Execution Attempts
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Smart contract bytecode may contain invalid operations: invalid opcodes, stack underflow/overflow, out-of-gas, invalid jump destinations, write to static context. EVM must catch all exceptional conditions, halt execution, revert state changes, and consume gas up to failure point. Exceptions must not propagate beyond EVM boundary or corrupt state.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Peers may send malformed blocks (invalid headers, incorrect Merkle roots, invalid transactions) or malformed protocol messages. EL must validate all fields before processing. Invalid data triggers exceptions (InvalidBlock, InvalidTransaction) which must result in message rejection, not node crash. Peer may be disconnected or penalized for repeated invalid messages.

RPC clients submit signed transaction bytes. EL must validate: valid RLP encoding, valid signature (recover signer), nonce matches account state, gas limit is reasonable, gas price is acceptable, sender has sufficient balance (value + gas). Validation failures return JSON-RPC errors with specific codes. Invalid transactions are rejected before mempool inclusion.

Smart contract execution may hit exceptional conditions: OutOfGasError (gas exhausted), StackUnderflowError (POP on empty stack), StackOverflowError (PUSH on 1024-item stack), InvalidOpcode (undefined opcode), InvalidJumpDest (JUMP to non-JUMPDEST), WriteInStaticContext (SSTORE in STATICCALL). All exceptions must halt execution, revert state changes, consume all provided gas (except for REVERT), and return error indication to caller. Exceptions must not leak across transaction boundaries or corrupt global state.
